title: FACT CHECK: No arrest warrant vs Sandro Marcos over Laos drug bust
summary: The misleading videos tie the Ilocos Norte lawmaker to a foiled shabu shipment, but there is no arrest warrant, case, or court order against him, contrary to the claim

blocks.text: Claim: An arrest warrant has been issued for Ilocos Norte 1st District Representative Sandro Marcos after he was linked to a foiled drug shipment from Laos.

Why we fact-checked this: A YouTube video posted on November 7 by the channel “News Update Files” is titled, “Arrest warrant ni Sandro nilabas na! Ikukulong na ang anak ni BBM? Sangkot pala sa dr*g shipment?”
(Arrest warrant for Sandro released! Will the son of [Bongbong Marcos] be jailed? Turns out he’s involved in the drug shipment?)
Its thumbnail shows a document stamped “arrest warrant” alongside an image of a crying man. Text overlaid on it reads, “Warrant nilabas na! Sandro ikukulong na? Arestado ang anak ni Bangag!”
(Warrant released! Will Sandro be jailed? Bangag’s son is arrested!)
A second video, posted on the same day by the channel “PoliTalak,” is titled “Heto na! Mananagot na sa batas! Sandro Marcos wala nang takas! Matinding utos ng Korte Suprema pirmado?”
(Here it is! He will be held accountable under the law! Sandro Marcos has no escape! A major Supreme Court order signed?)
As of writing, the two videos have garnered a combined 22,600 views and more than 160 likes.
The videos surfaced following reports last month of the attempted trafficking of 521 kilograms of shabu from Laos.

The facts: No court, government agency, or credible media report shows an arrest warrant for Marcos. None of the videos show proof of a warrant, case number, or court document, nor any evidence of the presidential son’s alleged link to the Laos drug bust.

Under the Philippine Constitution, a judge issues an arrest warrant after finding probable cause in a case filed in court. No complaint or case against the Ilocos Norte lawmaker over the drug shipment has been reported. Similarly, the Supreme Court has not issued any warrant for him.
Earlier fact checks also found no reports linking Sandro to the drug shipment.

In October, Rappler debunked a claim linking Sandro and former House speaker Martin Romualdez to the Laos drug bust. VERA Files later fact-checked a graphic claiming that the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency allegedly named him and the President as financiers of the drug smuggling attempt.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla has also rejected attempts to link the younger Marcos to the foiled drug shipment. Referring to the operation’s alleged financier, former Bangsamoro Transition Authority parliament member Edrieza Hadji Nasser Rimbang, Remulla said, “There is no connection between Rimbang and the President’s son.”
Marcos is not among the 11 persons of interest named in the case, either.
The Laos probe: On October 1, authorities intercepted 521 kilograms of suspected shabu, valued at P3.54 billion, at Luang Prabang airport on October 1.
Laotian authorities arrested Filipino national Fahad Mulok Dibarosan, Rimbang’s brother-in-law.
The Philippine National Police’s Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) said Rimbang financed the operation, a claim that Rimbang has denied.

On October 21, the CIDG said it was nearing completion of its case build-up and looking into charges under the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act. Police have asked the Anti-Money Laundering Council to trace the money trail, while the House also began its own investigation. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.
